title: Kernel ensemble stressbed and CI acceptance gates for prefill/decoder scheduling
creator: Asha Kulkarni
description:
Background: As the runtime adopts multiple kernel variants (float16, q4/8 variants, fused attention kernels) and more aggressive attention-optimization flags, we need a deterministic, reproducible stressbed that exercises realistic prefill and decode scheduling interactions. Existing bench suites capture bulk throughput, but not the cross-kernel/regime regressions that manifest only under mixed traffic and constrained KV cache warm starts.

Goal: Build a kernel-ensemble stressbed and CI acceptance gates that: (1) generates a compact but diverse corpus of prefill+decode traces reflecting production traffic slices; (2) systematically enumerates kernel selection combinations and attention opt flags; (3) runs ensemble stress experiments to capture tail latency, token-per-USD, and correctness deltas; (4) wires stable golden baselines and automated CI checks to catch regressions before rollout.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Golden baseline artifacts for 12 representative workload slices (short chat, long-context summarization, streaming decode, low-latency single-token) checked in and stored in the benchmark bucket.
- CI perf gate detects >=3% median or >=7% p99 latency regressions or >=5% token-cost regressions against golden within a PR run with synthetic replay anchors.
- Reproducible kernel-selection matrix runner that can run N(=10) seeds per config and produce a coverage report with kernel usage heatmaps and attention-op flag breakdown.
- Dashboard panel (Console) with per-gate history, flaky-run indicators, and triage links to the offending commit/PR.

Approach:
1) Workload corpus: curate and parametrize 12 slices from production traces (anonymized): prefix lengths, role-system prompts, average token churn, concurrency patterns. Provide deterministic seed files and a small generator to alter temperature/beam settings.
2) Ensemble runner: implement a lightweight harness that can launch the runtime against specific kernel selection overrides (env + config flags), attention optimization toggles (kv_cache_prio, fused_attention=true/false), and prefill/decode scheduling knobs (prefill_window, decode_batch_cap). Each run captures structured telemetry (latency histograms, token counts, kernel metadata emitted by runtime).
3) Golden baselines: capture golden metrics for each slice across our current release (runtime-1.21) and lock them with metadata: commit, binary SHA, hardware profile (A100-80GB, V100-32GB), and seed. Store as immutable artifacts in s3 with a registry file.
4) CI integration: add an acceptance job that runs a reduced subset (4 critical slices) and compares against golden using the same diff rules used by the harness. Fail PRs that exceed the thresholds. For full nightly runs, run the full 12-slice ensemble and post a triage report.
5) Telemetry & triage: extend telemetry exporters to include kernel-selection labels and attention-flag dimensions so the dashboard can attribute regressions to changes in kernel selection or attention optimizations.

Artifacts to land: harness repo changes, workload seed files (checked into bench-assets), golden registry JSON, CI job config (circleci/github actions), console dashboard panel PR, runbook for triage.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noise from hardware variance: mitigate by pinning hardware for golden capture and running N seeds to compute confidence intervals.
- Cost of CI: use reduced slice set for PRs and full run nightly; use sampling and caching of prefill states to lower token cost.
- Flaky kernels: introduce flaky-run detection (re-run x3) and mark experimental kernels behind feature flags.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: corpus curation + seed generation.
- Week 2: implement ensemble runner and basic telemetry labels.
- Week 3: capture golden baselines and CI PR job.
- Week 4: dashboard panel + rollout to nightly gate.

Acceptance criteria: golden artifacts present, CI gate enabled for PRs, dashboard shows historical trends, at least one regression caught in nightly job and triaged.

Links and references: design notes (confluence): /confluence/runtime/bench/ensemble, prior bench artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/goldens/, related Linear tickets: ENG-113842 (adaptive-kernel-telemetry-harness), ENG-21678 (quantile-latency-sentinel).
